newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BARCO FOCUS IN HOLIDAY-THINNED BRUSSELS.
newsitem.headline: BARCO FOCUS IN HOLIDAY-THINNED BRUSSELS.

text.p: News of a purchase by Belgian electronics group Barco was greeted with mixed feelings on the Brussels bourse on Friday, although investors still pushed the share higher in a broadly firmer market.
By 0850 GMT Barco was up 40 francs at 7,480 francs, although volume in Barco and other issues was thin due to a regional holiday in Flanders, where the company is based.
The Bel-20 share index, of which Barco is a component, was up 0.42 percent at 2,497.17 points.
One trader said the purchase could help Barco consolidate around 7,500 francs after recent strong gains.
"We could even see (Barco) going to 8,000 francs," he added.
Others, however, believed Barco was overvalued and the 700 million franc acquisition of digital signal encoder/decoder Danish Re did nothing to change that.

"Barco is still too expensive, even if this is quite a significant acquisition in terms of increasing the company's turnover. (The share) price has increased too much in recent months," Kurt Janssens of Nedee & Co said.
Generale Bank said in an investor note an acquisition was already discounted in Barco's price. It rated Barco a "hold".
"Based on the price only, Danish Re is not The Big Acquisition that Barco can afford and that it needs to maintain its growth momentum in coming years," Generale Bank said.
Barco had around 4.7 billion francs of cash at the end of 1996.
Analysts said they would be looking for the company to say more about the potential impact of the acquisition at a meeting with the company later on Friday.
Elsewhere, trade in non-ferrous metals company Union Miniere was calmer after two hectic days following an international private placement of a 24 percent stake in UM.
The placement by leading shareholder SGB sent UM's share's plunging from highs at around 3,800 francs to 3,400 francs, reportedly the price paid by a consortium of banks.
In early trade UM had risen five francs to 3,415 francs. Volume was a meagre 23,592 shares compared with around 400,000 shares traded on Thursday.
